title: Reserved Easement Appurtenant
subject: Real Property
stem:
On April 6, Martha owned Ridge Tract and Depot Tract. By warranty deed, Martha conveyed Depot Tract to Philip. The deed stated, "Martha reserves, for the benefit of Ridge Tract, an easement to use the gravel drive across Depot Tract to reach County Road 12." Martha retained Ridge Tract.

Philip later argues that he received Depot Tract free of any easement because a grantor may not reserve an interest in land being conveyed.

choices.A: The reservation is invalid because a grantor can never reserve an easement in land conveyed to another.
choices.B: The reservation is invalid because it appeared in the conveyance deed instead of in a separate easement instrument.
choices.C: The reservation created only a personal license that will terminate if Martha transfers Ridge Tract.
choices.D: The deed created a reserved easement appurtenant benefiting Ridge Tract and burdening Depot Tract.

rightExplanation: The deed created an easement appurtenant. A grantor may reserve an easement over land being conveyed when the reservation benefits land the grantor retains. The retained land is the dominant estate, and the conveyed land is the servient estate. The deed identifies Ridge Tract as the benefited parcel, Depot Tract as the burdened parcel, and the gravel drive as the route to the public road. That is enough to create a reserved easement appurtenant.

wrongExplanations.A: The argument tracks Philip's objection and sounds categorical. The breaker is that modern law permits a grantor to reserve an easement over conveyed land for retained land.
wrongExplanations.C: A personal license fits if the benefit belongs only to Martha. The breaker is that the deed makes Ridge Tract, not Martha personally, the benefited estate.
wrongExplanations.B: A separate document may create an easement. The breaker is that an express reservation can be made in the conveyance deed itself.
